For every fixed connected positive weighted loopless graph with n>=3 and a nonempty allowed missing-edge set under the stated iid focus workload, the sharp mr>=4 equality classification, uniform positivity/coercivity and strict convexity yield a unique optimal minimax strength for each edge. The continuum endpoint reduction and finite candidate comparison retain every global location tie and the single no-action option.

An endpoint-optimal strength need not be minimax: the exact344 example requires a balancing strength. This is a counterexample within the graph-general characterization, not a universal restoration-location assertion.

limitations: One fixed missing edge of arbitrary nonnegative strength, including t0=noaction, under iid Uniform/focus mixture on a closed interval below1. Randomized/adaptive/multiple-edge/cost/general-demand objectives are excluded.

Every graph is fixed, connected, loopless and positive weighted, with n>=3 and a finite nonempty allowed missing-edge set. Complete graphs with no admissible edge and point-mass zero-objective theta1 are excluded.

Analytic Dirichlet/equality, covariance/inverse, positive-rank, coercivity, strict-convexity and continuum endpoint/completeness bridges need separate audits; finite examples do not universally enumerate graphs or constitute Lean formalization.
